questionText: What is an import quota?
answers: A tax charged on each unit of a good that is imported
A payment the government makes to domestic producers
A limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported
A minimum price that domestic producers may charge

questionText: If the government increases the size of an import quota, what does this mean?
answers: A smaller quantity of the good may now be imported
A greater quantity of the good may now be imported
Domestic producers must now lower their prices
A tariff is charged on the good instead of a quota

questionText: A quota of 140,000 tonnes might suggest a price of $3, yet the price stays at $4. Why can a quota not push the price below $4?
answers: Because the government has fixed the price of beef at $4

title: Market for beef
questionText: The government sets the beef import quota to zero. What does this mean for the market?
answers: Beef imports become unlimited and the price falls to the world price

Beef may still be imported, but only at the world price
No beef may be imported, so the price rises to the domestic equilibrium and local producers supply the entire market
